newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London up on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London up on U.S. data.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London leapt higher on Friday led by lower-than expected U.S. Producer Price Index (PPI) figures which boosted T-bonds, traders said.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index was some 103.90 points firmer at 13,217.16 by 1411 GMT.

The Hong Kong Hang Seng, however, extended heavy losses to end depressed on Friday, down some 126.69 points at 13,113.26. It fell to two-month lows during early trading, bringing index losses for the week to 547.2 points, the highest weekly loss since March 1996.
"Hong Kong went its own direction against the trend of a strong Wall Street, one trader said. "But people are extremely nervous about selling or losing stock at these levels."

The U.S. PPI figures, used to measure wholesale inflation, fell by 0.3 percent in the face of analyst expectations that it would rise by around 0.2 percent. It was their first monthly decline since October 1994.
"The PPI figures saw the long bond rally again, which pushed the FTSE up, and HSBC seems to be back in form again," he said.

But traders said next week could see a turn around for Hong Kong. "We've probably seen the last of depressed selling (in Hong Kong)," one trader said, "If we close up around 100 points today, we should see a reasonable bounce of 100-150 points on Monday."
